papers.title: Robust solutions of uncertain linear programs
papers.abstract: Formulates static robust counterparts of uncertain linear programs under ellipsoidal and polyhedral uncertainty sets and derives tractable LP/SOCP reformulations.
key_results: Static robust counterpart for linear programs under polyhedral and ellipsoidal uncertainty
Tractable conic dualization of row-wise robust constraints

atlas_links.note: Row-wise conic dualization of ellipsoidal/SOC uncertainty sets.
Static robust LP baseline prior to adjustable recourse.

papers.title: Adjustable robust solutions of uncertain linear programs
papers.abstract: Introduces two-stage Adjustable Robust Counterpart (ARC) and Affinely Adjustable Robust Counterpart (AARC / ADR), proves RC = ARC under constraint-wise separable compact convex uncertainty PLUS compactness of feasible recourse sets V_u (Thm. 2.1, physical pp. 4-5), and gives finite LP reformulation of AARC on polytopes (Thm. 3.3).
key_results: Definition of fixed recourse, ARC, and AARC (affine decision rules)
Thm. 2.1 (physical pp. 4-5): RC = ARC under constraint-wise compact convex uncertainty Z = Z_1 x ... x Z_m AND compactness of the feasible recourse set V_u for every ARC-feasible first-stage u
Thm. 3.3: Finite LP reformulation of AARC over polyhedral uncertainty

atlas_links.note: Establishes fixed-recourse two-stage ARO formalism.
Thm. 2.1 (physical pp. 4-5): RC = ARC under constraint-wise compact convex uncertainty AND compactness of feasible recourse sets V_u for every ARC-feasible u.
Introduces the affine decision rule approximation whose exactness O1 seeks to characterize.

papers.title: Uncertain Linear Programs: Extended Affinely Adjustable Robust Counterparts
papers.abstract: Constructs an N-vs-1 separation between standard affine decision rules and adaptive optimum over the l1 cross-polytope and introduces Extended Affinely Adjustable Robust Counterparts (EAARC) via uncertainty lifting.
key_results: Examples 1-2 (p. 6): V_ADR = N vs V_ARO = 1 on the l1 cross-polytope
Lifted EAARC recovers V_EAARC = V_ARO = 1 exactly on the cross-polytope

atlas_links.note: Direct source of T3 counterexample (ADR=3 vs ARO=EAARC=1 for N=3).
Refutes any characterization predicting ADR exactness on l1 cross-polytopes.

papers.title: On the Power of Robust Solutions in Two-Stage Stochastic and Adaptive Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: Analyzes worst-case performance of static robust solutions relative to two-stage adaptive optimization and develops permutation-symmetry reductions for symmetric uncertainty sets.
key_results: Approximation bounds for static solutions in two-stage adaptive optimization
Symmetry-reduction lemmas for permutation-invariant uncertainty sets

atlas_links.note: Permutation-symmetry lemmas used in exact rational LP reduction of T5 (m=900).
Static vs two-stage adaptive performance gap baseline.

papers.title: Solving two-stage robust optimization problems using a column-and-constraint generation method
papers.abstract: Develops column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) for exact finite-step solution of two-stage robust linear programs over polyhedral uncertainty sets.
key_results: Finite-step convergence of C&CG over extreme points of polyhedral uncertainty

atlas_links.note: Extreme-point master problem structure closely related to finite vertex-LP reduction F4.

papers.title: Design of Near Optimal Decision Rules in Multistage Adaptive Mixed-Integer Optimization
papers.abstract: Studies multistage adaptive optimization with piecewise linear and binary decision rules and quantifies worst-case and empirical suboptimality gaps of linear rules.
key_results: Multistage piecewise linear decision rule architecture
Worst-case O(sqrt(k)) and empirical gap analysis for linear decision rules

atlas_links.note: Multistage decision-rule modeling relevant to k >= 2 closure generalization G1.

papers.title: A tight characterization of the performance of static solutions in two-stage adjustable robust linear optimization
papers.abstract: Gives a tight geometric characterization of the worst-case ratio between static and two-stage adaptive robust optimization via symmetry of the uncertainty set.
key_results: Thm. 3.2: Tight geometric performance bound rho(U) <= m for static vs adjustable ARO
Vertex-representation alone is insufficient for static/affine exactness

atlas_links.note: Bounds worst-case value of adaptivity (static vs single recourse stage).
Geometric characterization benchmark for static/affine gap.

papers.title: Duality in Two-Stage Adaptive Linear Optimization: Faster Computation and Stronger Bounds
authors: Frans J. C. T. de Ruiter
papers.abstract: Derives an equivalent dualized two-stage adaptive linear optimization reformulation and establishes conditions for exactness under box and simplex uncertainty sets.
key_results: Dualized two-stage ARO formulation with fewer variables/constraints
Exactness benchmarks for constraint-wise box and simplex uncertainty

atlas_links.note: Reference benchmark for T6 constraint-wise box exactness (p. 12).
Dual two-stage reformulation technique applicable to vertex-LP reduction.

papers.title: Decomposition for adjustable robust linear optimization subject to uncertainty polytope
papers.abstract: Studies exact vertex-based reformulations and decomposition for fixed-recourse two-stage ARO over polytopes and proves that vertex reduction fails under random recourse.
key_results: Exact extreme-point reformulation under fixed recourse on polytopes
Counterexample showing vertex reduction fails under random recourse (p. 6)

atlas_links.note: Polytope vertex reduction and convex interpolation for fixed-recourse ARO.

papers.title: A copositive approach for two-stage adjustable robust optimization with uncertain right-hand sides
papers.abstract: Proves exact copositive equivalence for fixed-recourse two-stage ARO, characterizes affine policies as inner cone IA(Q), and analyzes the SOC temporal network with Omega(s) affine gap.
key_results: Thm. equivalence & sandwich v_AR <= v_IB <= v_AP via copositive and IA(Q) cones
Section 4.1 temporal network on Euclidean ball B_2^s: V_ADR = s vs V_ARO = (s+sqrt(s))/2

atlas_links.note: Exact source of T2 SOC temporal network counterexample (arlp.tex lines 853-899).
Exact conic-membership characterization IA(Q) vs COP(Q) for ADR exactness.
Conic/SOC handling of non-polyhedral Euclidean-ball uncertainty.

papers.title: Conditions under which adjustability lowers the cost of a robust linear program
papers.abstract: Derives verifiable sufficient conditions under box uncertainty and fixed recourse for strict value of adjustability (V_static > V_ARO) via conflicting active constraints.
key_results: Prop. 1: Sufficient condition for strict value of adjustability under box uncertainty
Non-necessity examples where known static-exactness conditions fail yet values coincide

atlas_links.note: Directly informs verifiable sufficient conditions for strict measurement value V({r}) < V(empty).

papers.title: When are static and adjustable robust optimization problems with constraint-wise uncertainty equivalent?
papers.abstract: Generalizes constraint-wise static-adjustable equivalence to nonlinear convex robust optimization under compactness and convexity regularity assumptions.
key_results: Static = adjustable under constraint-wise compact convex uncertainty and convexity/concavity

atlas_links.note: Extends M1 constraint-wise equivalence beyond linear boxes.
Sion minimax conditions characterizing zero quantifier-order gap.

papers.title: A Tractable Approach for Designing Piecewise Affine Policies in Two-stage Adjustable Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Introduces affine domination for tractable piecewise affine policies with O(sqrt(m)) approximation guarantee and constructs an Omega(sqrt(m)) separating family for affine policies.
key_results: Eq. (ex:bad): Explicit fixed-recourse separating instance with Omega(sqrt(m)) ADR gap
Tractable piecewise affine dominance construction

atlas_links.note: Verbatim source of T5 separating family (m=900, V_ADR=1800/929 vs V_ARO<=1).
Rules out constant-factor or universal fixed-recourse ADR exactness.

papers.title: Adjustable Robust Optimization via Fourier-Motzkin Elimination
papers.abstract: Eliminates adjustable variables via Fourier-Motzkin projection to tighten linear decision rules and establishes exactness of linear rules over simplex uncertainty.
key_results: Fourier-Motzkin elimination reduces adjustable variables before applying ADR
Exactness of linear/affine decision rules on simplex uncertainty sets (p. 12)

atlas_links.note: Direct ground truth anchor for T7 simplex exactness.
Projection-based elimination to diagnose exactness of ADR.

papers.title: A Primal-Dual Lifting Scheme for Two-Stage Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Combines primal and dual uncertainty liftings to generate progressive inner (piecewise affine) and outer approximations of two-stage robust optimization problems.
key_results: Primal-dual lifting produces matching lower and upper bounds for two-stage ARO

atlas_links.note: Lifting-based piecewise affine selectors over polyhedral uncertainty.
Scalable primal-dual bounding template for multi-stage extensions.

papers.title: Generalized Farkas Lemma with Adjustable Variables and Two-Stage Robust Linear Programs
papers.venue: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications (2020)
papers.abstract: Proves a generalized adjustable Farkas lemma under closed-cone regularity conditions yielding exact conic dual reformulations for two-stage robust linear programs.
key_results: Adjustable Farkas lemma under closed-cone constraint qualification
Exact conic dual reformulation of two-stage robust LP (reformulation exactness)

atlas_links.note: Closed-cone regularity conditions directly governing strong duality in conic F3.

papers.title: On the Sparsity of Optimal Linear Decision Rules for a Class of Robust Optimization Problems with Box Uncertainty Sets
papers.abstract: Establishes that in multistage network inventory control under box uncertainty there always exists an optimal linear decision rule with O(ET) nonzero parameters instead of O(ET^2).
key_results: thm:main: O(ET) sparsity of optimal linear decision rules under box uncertainty

atlas_links.note: Structural sparsity of multistage box-uncertainty decision rules.

papers.title: Approximate Information States for Worst-Case Control and Learning in Uncertain Systems
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control / arXiv:2301.05089
papers.abstract: Develops exact and approximate information states for non-stochastic worst-case dynamic programming with partially observed states and bounded set-valued disturbances.
key_results: Information-state dynamic programming sufficient conditions for worst-case control
Quantifies loss when compressing observation history to state/information summaries

atlas_links.note: Formalizes exact vs lossy history compression for k >= 2 closure schedules.
Explains theoretically why merging prefixes loses predictive information state.

papers.title: Bounding the Optimal Number of Policies for Robust K-Adaptability
papers.abstract: Proves tight upper bounds on the number K of contingency policies needed for exact K-adaptability in two-stage robust optimization and proves NP-completeness of minimal K.
key_results: Thm. 2 & Thm. 11: Exact upper bounds on required policy count K
Thm. 29: Computing minimal exact K is NP-complete

atlas_links.note: Closest complexity benchmark (minimal policy count K vs minimal measurement schedule |R|).

papers.title: On the Optimality of Affine Decision Rules in Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Proves four sufficient conditions (F, A, D, B — inverse-positive M-matrix recourse with dominating constraints) for ADR optimality on arbitrary supports and gives minimal counterexamples for each condition.
key_results: Thm. 1 (p. 8): Conditions (F, A, D, B) imply exact ADR optimality on arbitrary supports
Prop. 1 (pp. 10, 45): Minimality counterexamples including 3/2 vs 5/4 for condition (B) and a non-necessity witness

atlas_links.note: Direct source of T4 counterexample (3/2 vs 5/4 on [-1, 1]).
Sharpest published sufficient condition (mechanism M2) and proof of non-necessity.

papers.title: When Is Two-Stage Sample Robust Optimization Asymptotically Optimal? A Simple Perspective
papers.abstract: Establishes combinatorial simplicity conditions on support polytopes for local linear feasibility in two-stage sample robust optimization and provides non-simple counterexamples.
key_results: Thm. 2: Simple polytope supports yield local linear feasibility
Thm. 4: Non-simple supports admit feasibility counterexamples

atlas_links.note: Combinatorial vertex-incidence perspective on linear feasibility vs value exactness.

papers.title: Optimal guaranteed control with one closure in linear nonstationary systems
papers.abstract: Formulates linear terminal optimal guaranteed control with one pre-specified state-measurement closure moment and explicitly notes that optimal placement of the closure moment remains open (p. 681).
key_results: Single-closure guaranteed control formulation and LP solution for fixed r
Explicit statement (p. 681) that choosing the optimal closure time r is an open problem

atlas_links.note: Primary school anchor explicitly posing optimal closure placement as open (p. 681).
Single-closure guaranteed control model foundation.

papers.title: Multiply-closed strategy in a linear terminal guaranteed-control problem
papers.venue: Trudy Instituta Matematiki i Mekhaniki UrO RAN 28(3):66-82
papers.abstract: Develops multiply-closed guaranteed control strategies for fixed schedules via parametric LP duality, demonstrates non-monotonic dependence of value on single closure time r (r=67 vs r=104), and notes minimax vs maximin contrast.
key_results: Parametric LP duality for fixed multi-closure schedules (p. 75)
Benchmark showing non-monotonic value dependence on single closure time r (p. 78)

atlas_links.note: Source benchmark instances r=67 and r=104 verified in bridge-transfer-v1.
Primary physical-page specification for BridgeFormalV2.Data.
Notes contrast between minimax and maximin guaranteed formulations.

papers.title: Optimal guaranteed control of linear systems with disturbances (Chapter 2, Dissertation)
papers.abstract: Systematizes the qualitative information ladder OC >= RO(k) >= DP (p. 39), proves polyhedral parametric closure-set representations (Thm. 2.1, Thm. 2.2, Lemma 2.5), and explicitly leaves optimal schedule placement outside scope (p. 75).
key_results: Qualitative information ladder OC >= RO(k) >= DP (p. 39)
Thm. 2.1, Thm. 2.2, Lemma 2.5: Polyhedral parametric representation and piecewise-affine supports
Explicitly leaves optimal schedule placement outside scope (p. 75)

atlas_links.note: Qualitative information ladder motivating monotonicity over enlarged schedules (p. 39).
Multi-closure polyhedral framework (Thm. 2.1-2.2) guiding G1 generalization.
Declares optimal closure placement open / outside scope (p. 75).
